newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Kerry Holdings raises loan to US$750 mln.
newsitem.headline: HK's Kerry Holdings raises loan to US$750 mln.

text.p: Kerry Holdings has increased the size of its loan facility to US$750 million from US$500 million after the issue was oversubscribed in the underwriting phase, the arrangers said Monday.
The issue was oversubscribed to over US$1.0 billion but scaled back.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, HSBC Investment Bank Asia and J.P. Morgan Securities Asia are coordinating arrangers.

Banks joining the facility may participate in either U.S. or Hong Kong dollars. The interest margin of the facility is 70 basis points per annum for U.S. dollars and 75 basis points per annum for Hong Kong dollars.
The facility is composed of two tranches.
The US$400 million tranche A is a straight term loan that will be used to refinance an outstanding US$400 million revolving credit dated December 18, 1995.
The US$350 million tranche B is a revolving credit for one year. Thereafter, the outstanding amount converts to a straight loan that repays at maturity.
Tranche B was increased from US$100 million after the oversubscription. Proceeds of the loan will be used for general corporate funding purposes of Kerry Holdings and its group companies.
With fees, the issue pays 84 basis points to top tier managers participating in U.S. dollars.

In addition to the coordinating arrangers, Bank of Nova Scotia, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Banque Nationale de Paris, Deutsche Bank, Fuji Bank, Industrial Bank of Japan, NatWest Markets, Paribas Asia, Sakura Bank, Societe Generale Asia, Sumitomo Bank and Westdeutsche Landesbank are senior arrangers and senior lead managers.
Bayerische Vereinsbank, Development Bank of Singapore, Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan, Rabobank, Sanwa Bank, Tokai Bank and Westpac Banking Corp are arrangers and lead managers.

Kerry Holdings, a member of Malaysian tycoon Robert Kuok's diversified group, has substantial interests in Hong Kong's Kerry Properties, Shangri-La Asia, Television Broadcasts and South China Morning Post (Holdings).
